To answer this question, we need to refer to the document "Sustainable recycling of cathode scraps via Cyrene-based separation" (susmat-2020).

According to the text in the document, the recovered NMC622 showed a discharge capacity of 158.0 mAh/g after 40 cycles at a charge/discharge rate of C/3.

This capacity is 100.9% of the capacity of the baseline sample after 40 cycles at the same rate.

Since the capacity of the baseline sample after 40 cycles is not explicitly stated in the text, we can calculate it by dividing the capacity of the baseline sample after the first four cycles (205.6 mAh/g) by 1.009 (which is 100.9% as a decimal). However, we are told that after 40 cycles the baseline capacity is 100.9% of the initial capacity of 205.6 mAh/g.

Thus the baseline capacity after 40 cycles is 205.6 mAh/g * 1.009 = 207.18 mAh/g

So the baseline capacity after 40 cycles is 207.18 mAh/g.
